description: §66.12.1 (non-mutating operations return new values) + §66.10 (aliases snapshot): `[0, ...a, 3]`, `a.concat([9])` and `[...b, ...c]` are NEW tapes built from their operands, which they leave unchanged. One #go click sets @n to 4 * 100 + 3 * 10 + 7 - 2 = 435.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S435 "type, and 1 both, 2 lift, 3 C, 4 suppress" (one sequence kind; non-mutating operations always allowed); ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S435 (dpa-052 item 1) "1 yes, 2 yes" (value semantics)
rationale: §66.12.1: "Non-mutating operations (`map`, `filter`, `slice`, `concat`, `find`, `some`, `every`, `reduce`, …) are always allowed; they return new values." §66.10 rule 2: "No write to a source is observable through a value taken from it earlier".
